ITQAN:v3p146/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p146/r4.speaker: الطيبي
ITQAN:v3p146/r4.claim: Al-Ṭībī's first type, concision by reduction, packs the letter's heading, content, and request into the few words of Solomon's message.
ITQAN:v3p146/r4.anchor: وقال الطيبي في التبيان الإيجاز الخالي من الحذف ثلاثة أقسام أحدها إيجاز القصر وهو أن يقصر اللفظ على معناه كقوله

ITQAN:v3p146/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p146/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p146/r5.claim: The author notes that calling a rhetorician's words molds for his meaning treats equality of wording and meaning as concision too.
ITQAN:v3p146/r5.anchor: وقيل في وصف بليغ كانت ألفاظه قوالب معناه قلت وهذا رأي من يدخل المساواة في الإيجاز

ELMALILI:27:21-31/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r15.claim: The wording suggests the letter was written in Arabic, since Sheba’s Himyarites were Arabs; it may instead have been written in Hebrew, with this text a translation or summary.
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r15.anchor: Bu ifadenin zâhirine nazaran mektup bu suretle Arapça yazılmıştır. Sebe’, Himyerîler Arap oldukları için demek ki Süleyman aleyhisselâm onlara mektubunu kendi lisanlarıyla yazmıştır.

ELMALILI:27:21-31/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r16.claim: Elmalılı allows that the original letter could have been in Hebrew, with the Arabic wording translating or summarizing its meaning.
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r16.anchor: Asıl mektubun İbranice yazılmış olup da bu onun tercemesi veya hulâsa-i mazmûnu olmak da muhtemildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r14.claim: To verify the hoopoe's report, Solomon sent a letter with it to the queen and instructed it to return with her response.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r14.anchor: yazdığı bir mektubu kraliçeye götürüp sonuçtan kendisini haberdar etmesini hüdhüde emretti.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r15.claim: The letter's basmala and its demand that Sheba's people submit to Solomon make the invitation both political and religious.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r15.anchor: Mektubun besmele ile başlaması ve Sebe’ halkının Süleyman’a teslim olmalarını istemesi, davetin hem siyasî hem de dinî olduğunu göstermektedir.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r7.claim: The queen summarized the letter as being from Solomon and beginning in God’s name, rather than reading it all aloud.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r7.anchor: the letter is from Solomon (sws) and begins with the name of the merciful God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r1.claim: Since the queen only summarized the letter, she named its sender and opening; ancient royal letters and decrees conventionally began by naming sender and recipient.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r1.anchor: for this reason she only told them the name of the sender and the manner in which it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r2.claim: The queen’s emphasis on the letter’s opening illuminates the history of the basmala and conveys the seriousness of its spirit.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r2.anchor: special importance to the be ginning of the letter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r4.claim: Although she summarized it, ancient letters were concise, as Prophet Muhammad’s letters show, so Solomon’s letter may have contained only the words she reported.

BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r1.claim: Bilqis's wording answers the implied questions of who sent the letter and what it contains.
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r1.anchor: كأنه قيل : ممن هو وماذا مضمونه؟ فقالت : إنه من سليمان

BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r2.claim: An esoteric letter-by-letter reading assigns ba to permanence, sin to splendor, mim to sovereignty, alif to oneness, the two lams to beauty and majesty, and ha to divine identity.
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r2.anchor: الباء بقاؤه والسين سناؤه والميم ملكه والألف أحديته واللامان جماله وجلاله والهاء هويته

BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r3.claim: In this reading, al-Rahman signifies mercy to all people in this world and the next, while al-Rahim signifies special mercy in the next world.
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r3.anchor: الرحمان إشارة إلى رحمته لأهل العموم في الدنيا والآخرة والرحيم إشارة إلى رحمته لأهل الخصوص في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r4.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r4.claim: Some great Sufis say this is, in truth, the basmala of Bara'a; because its people were disavowed, it was bestowed on the animals who believed in Solomon.
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r4.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : إنها بسملة براءة في الحقيقة ولكن لما وقع التبري من أهلها أعطيت للبهائم التي آمنت بسليمان

BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r5.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r5.claim: The opening ba suffices because every existent thing is encompassed by God's general or particular mercy.
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r5.anchor: واكتفى في أول السورة بالباء إذ كل شيء في الوجود الكوني لا يخلو من رحمة الله عامة أو خاصة

BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r6.claim: This basmala is not a complete verse like the basmala in Hud, whereas the basmalas opening surahs are separate verses revealed 114 times, once for each surah.
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r6.anchor: وهذه البسملة ليست بآية تامة مثل : {بسم الله مجارااها ومرسااهآ} (هود : 41)

BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r7.speaker: المولى الجامي
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r7.claim: Jami's Persian couplet says the basmala's nineteen letters pour abundant grace over seventeen thousand worlds.
BURSEVI:v6p249#3/r7.anchor: قال المولى الجامي في حق البسملة : نوزده حرفست كه هده هزار عالم ازو يافته فيض عميم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81#2/r1.claim: Qatadah says people wrote only “In Your name, O Allah” until Solomon’s letter introduced the full basmala.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81#2/r1.anchor: عبد الرزاق عن معمر عن قتادة قال لم يكن الناس يكتبون إلا باسمك اللهم حتى نزلت ﴿ إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ﴾

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81#2/r2.speaker: الشعبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81#2/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reports that the Prophet’s written invocation progressed through shorter forms before the full basmala was revealed with Solomon’s letter.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81#2/r2.anchor: عن الشعبي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كتب أول ما كتب باسمك اللهم حتى نزلت ﴿ بسم الله مجراها ومرساها ﴾

QASHANI:27:28-31/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:28-31/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:28-31/r3.claim: Solomon's name points to the Essence that grants preparedness, faculties by which potential is actualized in intellect, and fitting perfection in moral qualities and attributes.
QASHANI:27:28-31/r3.anchor: بإفاضة الاستعداد وما يخرج به ما فيه إلى العقل من الآلات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r8.claim: The apparent letter text begins with من سليمان and then God's name; Solomon may have placed his own name first as protection in case the unbelieving queen acted improperly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن بداءة الكتاب من سليمان باسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، إلى آخر ما قص الله منه خاصة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r9.claim: Alternatively, من سليمان may have been an outside heading, with the basmala and remaining text inside.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r9.anchor: أو كان عنوانا في ظاهر الكتاب، وباطنه فيه بسم الله إلى آخره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r10.claim: Alternatively, the basmala came first in writing, but Bilqis put من سليمان first when recounting the letter after reading it privately.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r10.anchor: واحتمل أن يكون مؤخرا في الكتابة عن بسم الله، وإن ابتدأ الكتاب باسم الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r11.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r11.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi says earlier messengers customarily began their letters by naming themselves as sender.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r11.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن العربي: كانت رسل المتقدمين إذا كتبوا كتابا بدأوا بأنفسهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r12.speaker: أنس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r12.claim: Anas reports that the Companions began their letters to the Prophet with their own names, since no one was more honored than he.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r12.anchor: وعن أنس: ما كان أحد أعظم حرمة من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r13.speaker: أبو الليث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r13.claim: Abu al-Layth says beginning with the addressee is also valid, by communal consensus and practice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r13.anchor: وقال أبو الليث في (كتاب البستان) له: ولو بدأ بالمكتوب إليه جاز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r14.claim: Most readers pronounce both إنّه clauses with kasra; ʿAbd Allāh adds a conjunction before the second clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r14.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: إنه من سليمان، وإنه بكسر الهمزة فيهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r15.speaker: عكرمة، وابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r15.claim: ʿIkrima and Ibn Abi ʿAbla read both hamzas with fatḥa, parsing the clauses as an apposition or as an explanation of the letter's nobility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r15.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة، وابن أبي عبلة: بفتحهما، وخرج على البدل من كتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r16.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r16.claim: Ubayy reads أن من سليمان وأن بسم الله with fatḥa and a silent nūn, parsed either as explanatory or as a lightened emphatic particle with its pronoun omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r16.anchor: وقرأ أبي: أن من سليمان وأن بسم الله، بفتح الهمزة ونون ساكنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p235/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p235/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p235/r1.claim: The basmala is a noble, eloquent and meaningful opening for books in every language and religious law.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p235/r1.anchor: شريف بارع المعنى مبدوء به في الكتب في كل لغة وكل شرع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p235/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p235/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p235/r16.claim: A report says no one before Solomon had written بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p235/r16.anchor: وروي أنه لم يكتب أحد بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قبل سليمان

QUSHAYRI:v2p417/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p417/r1.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v2p417/r1.claim: The letter was considered noble because it began with the basmala.
QUSHAYRI:v2p417/r1.anchor: لأنه كان مصدرا ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

QUSHAYRI:v2p417/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p417/r2.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v2p417/r2.claim: Another explanation of its nobility is that it named God first rather than using a sender-and-recipient formula such as “from Solomon to so-and-so.”
QUSHAYRI:v2p417/r2.anchor: كتب فيه اسم نفسه أولا ولم يقل : إنه من سليمان إلى فلانة

QUSHAYRI:v2p417/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p417/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p417/r5.claim: If the letter is noble because it contains the basmala, prayer is noble when it retains the naming formula and deficient when stripped of it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p417/r5.anchor: فالكريم من الصلاة ما لا يتجرد عن التسمية . وإذا تجردت كان الأمر فيها بالعكس

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r1.claim: The repeated emphatic إنّ answers an implicit question about the letter’s sender and contents, so its emphatic force is apt even if the question is only inferred.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r1.anchor: فلذاك أيضا أولوقوعه في جواب سؤال مقدر كأنه قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r2.claim: The first pronoun in إنه refers to the letter, while the second refers to its unmentioned contents.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r2.anchor: ويعلم مما ذكر أن ضمير ( إنه ) الأول للكتاب وضمير ( إنه ) الثاني للمضمون وإن لم يذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r3.claim: The verse does not prove that Solomon put his own name before God’s name; the queen may have learned the sender from his signature after the basmala.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r3.anchor: وليس في الآية ما يدل على أنه عليه السلام قدم اسمه على اسم الله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r4.speaker: يزيد بن رومان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r4.claim: Ibn Abī Ḥātim reports that Solomon’s letter began with the basmala, then identified him as Solomon son of David and addressed Bilqīs and her people.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r4.anchor: وقد أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن يزيد بن رومان أنه قال : كتب سليمان بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم من سليمان ابن داود

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r5.claim: An alternative reading takes the first إنه as the letter’s heading: Solomon titled the letter with his own name before the basmala.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r5.anchor: وقيل : ضمير ( انه ) الأول للعنوان وأنه عليه السلام عنون الكتاب باسمه مقدما له

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān favors the heading interpretation and suggests Solomon put his name first to shield God’s name if the unbelieving queen behaved disrespectfully.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r6.anchor: واستظهر هذا أبو حيان ثم قال : وقدم عليه السلام اسمه لاحتمال أن يبدر منها ما يليق

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī dismisses Abū Ḥayyān’s proposed protective reason as unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r7.anchor: فيكون اسمه وقاية لاسم الله عز وجل وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r8.claim: After this verse was revealed, opening letters with the basmala became the Prophet’s established practice without disagreement.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r8.anchor: وكتابة البسملة في أوائل الكتب مما جرت به سنة نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد نزول هذه الآية بلا خلاف

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r9.speaker: الشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r9.claim: A report from al-Shaʿbī says people formerly wrote “In Your name, O God”; the Prophet retained that formula until 11:41, then used “In the name of God,” then 17:110 led to the longer formula, and this verse to the full basmala.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r9.anchor: عن الشعبي قال : كان أهل الجاهلية يكتبون باسمك اللهم فكتب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو ما كتب باسمك اللهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r10.speaker: أبو مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r10.claim: Abū Dāwūd’s Mursal report from Abū Mālik likewise says the Prophet wrote “In Your name, O God” until this verse, after which he wrote “In the name of God.”
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r10.anchor: وأخرج أبو داود في مراسيله عن أبي مالك قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يكتب باسمك اللهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r11.speaker: ميمون بن مهران وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r11.claim: Similar accounts are also transmitted from Maymūn ibn Mihrān and Qatāda.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r11.anchor: وروي نحو ذلك عن ميمون بن مهران وقتادة وهذا عندي مما لايكاد يتسنى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r12.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds the reported chronology nearly impossible if the basmala was revealed before this verse, and says that earlier-revelation position should not be opposed.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r12.anchor: وهذا عندي مما لايكاد يتسنى مع القول بنزول البسملة قبل نزول هذه الآية وهذا القول مما لاينبغي أن يذهب إلى خلافه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r13.speaker: الجلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r13.claim: Al-Suyūṭī lists 96:1 as the soundest first-revelation view, alongside views naming al-Muddaththir, al-Fātiḥa, or the basmala.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r13.anchor: فقد قال الجلال السيوطي في اتقانه اختلف في أول ما نزل من القرآن على أقوال أحدها وهو الصحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r14.speaker: الجلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r14.claim: Al-Suyūṭī argues that the basmala need not count as a separate first-revelation opinion, since each sūra’s revelation necessarily includes its basmala; Al-Ālūsī accepts that this places it first absolutely.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195/r14.anchor: فانه من ضرورة نزول السورة نزول البسملة معها فهي أول آية نزلت على الاطلاق

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r1.claim: If the basmala was the first revelation and the opening of God’s Book, it was fitting for the Prophet to open his letters with it as well.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r1.anchor: فان البسملة إذا كانت أول آية نزلت كانت هي المفتتح لكتاب الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r2.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r2.claim: Some eminent scholars recommend writing the basmala on a line by itself in letters and books.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r2.anchor: وذكر بعض الأجلة أنها إذا كتبت في الكتب والرسائل فالأولى أن تكتب سطرا وحدها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r3.speaker: الصولي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṣūlī’s scribal manual recommends starting at the page margin, aligning the following prayer with the basmala, avoiding a short spill beyond it, and not centering it.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r3.anchor: وفي أدب الكتاب للصولي أنهم يختارون أن يبدأ الكاتب بالبسملة من حاشية القرطاس ثم يكتب الدعاء مساويا لها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r4.claim: Adding a prayer after the basmala was not an early practice; early letters simply named the sender and recipient.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r4.anchor: وما ذكر من كتابة الدعاء بعدها لم يكن في الصدر الأول وإنما كان فيه كتابة من فلان إلى فلان

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r5.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r5.claim: Anas reports that, despite the Prophet’s supreme honor, his Companions began letters to him by naming themselves first.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r5.anchor: ففي البحر عن أنس ما كان أحد أعظم حرمة من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان أصحابه إذا كتبوا اليه كتابا بدؤا بأنفسهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r6.speaker: أبو الليث
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r6.claim: Abū al-Layth says it is also permissible to name the recipient first because the community has agreed to and practiced that order.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو الليث في البستان له : ولو بدأ بالمكتوب اليه جاز لأن الأمة قد اجتمعت عليه وفعلوه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r7.claim: The verse’s wording suggests the basmala was not unique to Solomon, though some say its specific Arabic wording and order were unique; Al-Ālūsī considers that possible because Solomon’s original was translated for us.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r7.anchor: وظاهر الآية أن البسملة ليست من الخصوصيات وقال بعضهم : إنها منها لكن باللفظ العربي والترتيب المخصوص

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r8.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r8.claim: ʿAbd Allāh read وإنه من سليمان with an added conjunction; Abū Ḥayyān parses the conjunction as coordinating with إني ألقي, while another view makes it circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ( وإنه من سليمان ) بزيادة واو وخرجه أبو حيان على أنها عاطفة للجملة بعدها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r9.speaker: عكرمة وابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r9.claim: ʿIkrima and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read both instances with fatḥa on أن; they can be parsed as apposition to كتاب or as causal clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة وابن أبي عبلة ( أنه من سليمان وأنه ) بفتح همزة أن في الموضعين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r10.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r10.claim: Ubayy read أن من سليمان وأن بسم الله with fatḥa and a still nūn; the first أن can explain the preceding speech or be a lightened form of the emphatic particle.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p195#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( أن منسليمان وأن بسم الله ) بفتح الهمزة وسكون النون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159#2/r1.claim: Bilqis identifies the letter as being from Solomon and says it begins with the basmala.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159#2/r1.anchor: {إنه من سليمان} وبينت المكتوب فقالت: {وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم}

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r4.claim: The declaration that the letter is from Solomon resumes as though someone asked who sent it and what it says; it can refer to the letter or its heading, then to the text or its content.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r4.anchor: استئناف كأنه قيل لها ممن هو وما هو فقالت إنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r5.claim: An alternate reading with fatḥa on inna makes the phrase an apposition to كتاب or explains why it is noble.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r5.anchor: وقرىء بالفتح على الإبدال من { كتاب }

BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r6.claim: Naming Solomon before the basmala does not detract from beginning with praise of God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r6.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن الابتداء باسم صاحب الكتاب لا يقدح في الابتداء بالحمد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r7.claim: The basmala praises the supreme God, whose majesty and generosity encompass all and whose mercy grants special favors to whom He wills.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r7.anchor: فحمد المستحق للحمد وهو الملك الأعلى المحيط عظمه بدائرتي الجلال والإكرام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r8.claim: After identifying the sender, the basmala names God as the one worthy of worship and signals Solomon's prophethood; this order favors acceptance because most people recognize truth through people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r8.anchor: لأن أكثر الخلق إنما يعرف الحق بالرجال , ولما في كتابه من الدلالة على نبوته

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the hoopoe carried the letter to the middle of the queen’s throne, dropped it to her, and she read Solomon’s message.
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {اذهب بكتابي هذا} قال: كتب معه بكتاب فقال {اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم ثم تول عنهم}

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r13.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r13.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that the letter contained only the words about Solomon and the basmala recited in the Qur’an.
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r13.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} قال: لم يزد زعموا [] على هذا الكتاب على ما قص الله

DURR-FULL:v6p353/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r1.speaker: يزيد بن رومان
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r1.claim: Yazid ibn Ruman gives the letter’s wording as the basmala followed by Solomon’s name and his address to Bilqis, daughter of Dhi Sharh, and her people.
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r1.anchor: عن يزيد بن رومان قال: كتب بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم من سليمان بن داود إلى بلقيس بنت ذي شرح وقومها

DURR-FULL:v6p353/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r2.claim: Mujahid transmits the fuller letter: it is from God’s servant Solomon to the queen of Sheba, gives peace to followers of guidance, and commands her not to be arrogant and to come submitting.
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: أن سليمان بن داود كتب إلى ملكة سبأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم من عبد الله سليمان بن داود إلى بلقيس ملكة سبأ

DURR-FULL:v6p353/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r3.claim: Mujahid says Solomon’s letter to the queen contained no more than the wording preserved in the Qur’an.
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: لم يكن في كتاب سليمان إلى صاحبة سبأ إلا ما تقرأون في القرآن

DURR-FULL:v6p353/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r6.speaker: سفيان بن منصور
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r6.claim: Sufyan ibn Mansur transmits the saying that Solomon was the most eloquent in writing and the most concise.
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r6.anchor: من طريق سفيان بن منصور قال: كان يقال كان سليمان بن داود أبلغ الناس في كتاب وأقله كلاما

DURR-FULL:v6p353/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r7.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbi describes the basmala’s development in correspondence: people and the Prophet first wrote “in Your name, O God,” then the revealed forms progressed from “in God’s name” to “in God’s name, the Merciful,” and finally the complete basmala.
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r7.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: كان أهل الجاهلية يكتبون باسمك اللهم فكتب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أول ما كتب: باسمك اللهم

DURR-FULL:v6p353/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r8.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r8.claim: Al-Harith al-Akli recounts al-Shaʿbi’s account of the same staged change in the Prophet’s written basmala, ending with the complete formula after this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v6p353/r8.anchor: الحرث العكلي قال: قال لي الشعبي: كيف كان كتاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إليكم قلت: باسمك اللهم

DURR-FULL:v6p354/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p354/r1.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
DURR-FULL:v6p354/r1.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran says the Prophet continued writing “in Your name, O God” until this verse revealed the full basmala.
DURR-FULL:v6p354/r1.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يكتب (باسمك اللهم) حتى نزلت {إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم}

DURR-FULL:v6p354/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p354/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p354/r2.claim: Qatada says people wrote only “in Your name, O God” until this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v6p354/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قال: لم يكن الناس يكتبون إلا (باسمك اللهم) حتى نزلت {إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم}

DURR-FULL:v6p354/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p354/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v6p354/r3.claim: Abu Malik says the Prophet changed from “in Your name, O God” to the full basmala when this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v6p354/r3.anchor: عن أبي مالك قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يكتب (باسمك اللهم) فلما نزلت {إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} كتب (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم)

DURR-FULL:v6p354/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p354/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
DURR-FULL:v6p354/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib reports the Prophet’s invitation to Kisra, Caesar, and the Negus to worship God alone; Caesar remarked that this basmala-marked letter was unlike any he had seen since Solomon’s.
DURR-FULL:v6p354/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال: كتب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى كسرى وقيصر والنجاشي أما بعد: فتعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the queen opened the letter, found it was from Solomon, and saw the basmala inside.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r1.anchor: عن السدي اني القي الي كتاب كريم انه من سليمان فلما فتحته وجدته من سليمان

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r2.speaker: يزيد بن رومان
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r2.claim: Yazid ibn Ruman says the letter was from Solomon son of David to Balqis daughter of Dhi Sharh and her people, beginning with the basmala.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق ، عن يزيد بن رومان انه من سليمان وانه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قال كتب معه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم من سليمان بن داود إلى بلقيس

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r3.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r3.claim: Maimun ibn Mihran reports that the Prophet used to write “In Your name, O God”; when Arabs questioned al-Rahman, God revealed the instruction to call Him by either name.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r3.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يكتب باسمك اللهم حين نزلت انه من سليمان وانه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r4.speaker: الشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says pre-Islamic Arabs wrote “In Your name, O God”; the Prophet adopted the full basmala after the verse allowing invocation of Allah or al-Rahman was revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r4.anchor: عن الشعبي قال : كان اهل الجاهلية يكتبون باسمك اللهم فكتب النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ولم يسم الله فلما نزلت قل ادعوا الله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says Solomon's letter to the queen of Sheba contained only the wording about its being from Solomon and beginning in God's name preserved in the Qur'an.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : لم يكن في كتاب سليمان إلى صاحبه سبا الا ما روي في القران انه من سليمان وانه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r6.speaker: بريدة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r6.claim: Burayda reports the Prophet saying he knew a verse not given to any prophet before Solomon, then identifying this verse as the letter's opening formula.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872#2/r6.anchor: عن أبيه قال : كنت امشي مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : اني اعلم آية لم تنزل على نبي قبلي بعد سليمان بن داود

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r1.claim: Qatada interprets “do not exalt yourselves over me” as “do not oppose me.”
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : الا تعلوا علي الا تخالفوا علي

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r2.claim: Al-Suddi explains the words as “do not dare defy me, and come to me submitting.”
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r2.anchor: عن السدي الا تعلوا علي يقول : لا تجرئوا علي واتوني مسلمين

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r3.speaker: سفيان
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r3.claim: Sufyan glosses the command as “do not refuse me.”
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r3.anchor: عن سفيان الا تعلوا علي يقول : لا تابوا علي

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r4.speaker: زهير بن محمد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r4.claim: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad glosses the command as “do not disobey me.”
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r4.anchor: ثنا زهير بن محمد في قول الله : الا تعلوا علي يقول : لا تعصوني .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r5.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says refusal of Solomon's invitation would bring war; when asked, he also affirms that the wording means not to act arrogantly toward him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r5.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم في قول الله : الا تعلوا قال : تمتنعوا من الذي دعوتكم اليه ان امتنعتم جاهدتكم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r6.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r6.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd accepts “do not exalt yourselves over me” as meaning “do not be arrogant toward me.”
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r6.anchor: قيل له : الا تعلوا علي الا تتكبروا علي ، قال : نعم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says “come to me as Muslims” means as monotheists.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس مسلمين يقول : موحدين

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r8.speaker: زهير بن محمد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r8.claim: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad says “come to me as Muslims” means sincerely devoted.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r8.anchor: ثنا زهير بن محمد واتوني مسلمين يقول : مخلصين .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r9.speaker: سفيان
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r9.claim: Sufyan says “come to me as Muslims” means obediently.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r9.anchor: عن سفيان في قوله : واتوني مسلمين قال : طائعين

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r10.claim: Qatada says prophets wrote in concise phrases and did not elaborate or overlengthen their letters.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r10.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : الا تعلوا علي واتوني مسلمين قال : وكذلك كان يكتب الانبياء جملا لا يسهبون

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r11.speaker: منصور
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r11.claim: Mansur reports the saying that Solomon was the most eloquent letter writer and the briefest, illustrated by this concise letter.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2873/r11.anchor: عن منصور قال كان يقال : كان سليمان بن داود ابلغ الناس في كتاب ، واقله املاء ثم قرا

FARRA:v2p291/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p291/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p291/r9.claim: Both instances of inna are read with kasra; opening them with fatḥa is also grammatical, with their positions analyzed as apposition or as accusatives after an omitted preposition.

FARRA:v2p291/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p291/r10.speaker: أبي
FARRA:v2p291/r10.claim: Ubayy’s reading has wa-an before the basmala, which supports opening the particle; an opened an joined to a clause is lightened.
FARRA:v2p291/r10.anchor: في قراءة أبي (وأن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم)

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r6.claim: If “noble” means it began with God’s name, the letter is complete rather than deficient; a Prophetic report says speech without the basmala is deficient.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r6.anchor: ف كريم ضد أجذم كما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «كل كلام لم يبدأ باسم الله تعالى فهو أجذم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r7.claim: The letter may reproduce concise, eloquent wording: address first, then God’s name, then a command against arrogance and for submission.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r7.anchor: فيحتمل اللفظ أنه نص الكتاب موجزا بليغا وكذلك كتب الأنبياء وقدم فيه العنوان وهي عادة الناس على وجه الدهر، ثم سمى الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r8.claim: Alternatively, the Queen may have summarized the letter’s meanings rather than its exact sequence, naming Solomon and explaining its message.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أنها قصدت إلى اقتضاب معانيه دون ترتيبه فأعلمتهم إنه من سليمان وأن معنى ما فيه كذا وكذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r9.speaker: أبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r9.claim: Ubayy reads “wa-an bismi Allāh” with fatḥa on the hamza, light nūn, and omission of the hāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبي «وأن بسم الله» بفتح الهمز وتخفيف النون وحذف الهاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r10.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r10.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads “annahu” with fatḥa on both hamzas.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة «أنه» من «وأنه» بفتح الهمزة فيهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r11.speaker: عبد الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r11.claim: The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh adds a wāw before “it is from Solomon.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r11.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله «وأنه من سليمان» بزيادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r12.claim: The basmala is an exceptionally noble, richly meaningful opening expressed across languages and religious traditions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r12.anchor: وبسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، استفتاح شريف بارع المعنى معبر عنه بكل لغة وفي كل شرع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p168/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p168/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p168/r1.claim: The first pronoun identifies the letter as from Solomon; the second says its writing begins “In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p168/r1.anchor: أي إن الكتاب من عنده وإنه أي وإن المكتوب بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r1.claim: The recipients recognize the letter as from God's prophet Solomon and know they cannot oppose him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r1.anchor: فعرفوا أنه من نبي الله سليمان، وأنه لا قبل لهم به.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r2.claim: The letter is exceptionally eloquent, concise, and clear, expressing its meaning in the simplest and best wording.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r2.anchor: وهذا الكتاب في غاية البلاغة والوجازة والفصاحة، فإنه حصل المعنى بأيسر عبارة وأحسنها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r3.speaker: العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r3.claim: Scholars say no one before Solomon wrote 'In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.'
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r3.anchor: قال العلماء: ولم يكتب أحد {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} قبل سليمان، عليه السلام.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r4.claim: A report from Burayda attributes to the Prophet the statement that he knew a verse not revealed to a prophet before him after Solomon, then identifies the basmala in Solomon's letter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r4.anchor: عن أبيه قال: كنت أمشي مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir grades the report about the verse as strange with a weak chain.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r6.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r6.claim: Maimun ibn Mihran says the Prophet wrote 'In Your name, O God' until this verse came, after which he wrote the full basmala.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188#2/r6.anchor: وقال ميمون بن مهران: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكتب: باسمك اللهم، حتى نزلت هذه الآية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r5.claim: The basmala resumes and explains the letter's contents: the hearers are told who sent it and what it says.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r5.anchor: قيل : مصدر ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم : هو استئناف وتبيين لما ألقى إليها ، كأنا لما قالت : إني ألقى إلي كتاب كريم ، قيل لها : ممن هو ؟ وما هو ؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r6.speaker: عبد الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r6.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads the clause with a conjunction, linking 'it is from Solomon' and 'it is' to the queen's prior statement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله : ( وإنه من سليمان وإنه ) عطفا على : إني .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r7.claim: Another reading opens the hamza in both clauses, making them appositional to 'a letter'; alternatively they explain why it is noble, since it is from Solomon and begins with God's name.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r7.anchor: وقرىء : ( أنه من سليمان وأنه ) ، بالفتح على أنه بدل من كتاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r8.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r8.claim: Ubayy reads 'that it is from Solomon and that in the name of God,' with أن as explanatory; أن in ألا تعلوا is explanatory as well.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبي : ( أن من سليمان وأن بسم الله ) ، على أن المفسرة . وأن في { ألا تعلوا } مفسرة أيضا .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r10.claim: An account gives the letter's text from Solomon son of David to Bilqis: greeting to those who follow guidance, followed by a command not to exalt themselves and to come submitting; prophetic letters were concise, scented with musk, and sealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r10.anchor: يروى أن نسخة الكتاب من عبد الله سليمان بن داود إلى بلقيس ملكة سبأ : السلام على من اتبع الهدى ، أما بعد : فلا تعلوا علي وائتوني مسلمين ، وكانت كتب الأنبياء عليهم السلام جملا لا يطيلون

NAHHAS:v3p208/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p208/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p208/r3.claim: ‘It is from Solomon’ may introduce the letter’s contents or its opening formula, ‘In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful.’
NAHHAS:v3p208/r3.anchor: أي وأن الكلام أو أن مبتدأ الكلام بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

NAHHAS:v3p208/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p208/r4.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p208/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ permits both hamzas in ‘it is from Solomon and it is…’ to take fatḥa, either as a nominative construction after ‘it was delivered to me’ or as accusative after an omitted preposition.
NAHHAS:v3p208/r4.anchor: وأجاز الفراء ( أنه من سليمان وأنه ) بفتحهما جميعا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r7.claim: The queen identifies the sender and explains who sent the letter by saying it is from Solomon.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r7.anchor: أما قولها إنه من سليمان فلإعلامهم مرسل الكتابي وممن هو

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r8.claim: The invocation was unfamiliar to the queen and her people; Solomon was the first to begin with the full formula.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r8.anchor: فلاستنكار هذا الاستفتاح الذي لم تعرفه هي ولا قومها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r9.speaker: رسول الله ﷺ
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r9.claim: In a report from Ibn Burayda’s father, the Prophet says he knows a verse not revealed to a prophet before him after Solomon.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r9.anchor: كنت أمشي مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : ( إني لأعلم آية لم تنزل على نبي قبلي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r10.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r10.claim: Al-Shaʿbī recounts that the Prophet’s opening formulas developed from “In Your name, God” through shorter forms to the full basmala after these verses were revealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r10.anchor: حكى عاصم عن الشعبي قال : كانت كتب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعة كتب

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r11.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r11.claim: After ʿĀṣim says he saw the Prophet’s letter with the full basmala, al-Shaʿbī calls that formula the third book form.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r11.anchor: قال عاصم قلت للشعبي أنا رأيت كتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم . { بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم } قال ذلك الكتاب الثالث

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r12.claim: Prophetic letters are concise calls to obedience, without extended explanation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r12.anchor: فهذه كتب الأنباء موجزة مقصورة على الدعاء إلى الطاعة من غير بسط ولا إسهاب

MUQATIL:27:27-32/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r7.claim: The letter contained only the statement that it was from Solomon, the basmala, a prohibition against exalting themselves over him, and a demand to come submitting.
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r7.anchor: فأخبرتهم بما فى الكتاب، ولم يكن فيه شىء غير: " إنه من سليمان، وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

MUQATIL:27:27-32/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r10.claim: She identifies the letter as from Solomon and notes its opening with the basmala.
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r10.anchor: إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p211/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211/r1.claim: The statement explains what was in the letter: after calling it noble, the queen identifies its sender and contents.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211/r1.anchor: هو تبيين لما ألقى إليها كأنها لما قالت أني ألقى إلى كتاب كريم قيل لها ممن هو وما هو

QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r6.claim: A report says no one before Solomon wrote Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim; Abdullah's reading adds a waw before the statement that it is from Solomon.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r6.anchor: وقد روي أنه لم يكتب بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم أحد قبل سليمان. وفي قراءة عبد الله { وإنه من سليمان } بزيادة واو.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r1.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r1.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says ʿaziz is an epithet for the Qur'an alone; use العالي instead in correspondence to honor authority and preserve religious reverence.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r1.anchor: فاجتنبوها في كتبكم، واجعلوا بدلها العالي توفية لحق الولاية، وحياطة للديانة قاله القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r2.speaker: الربيع عن أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r2.claim: Anas reports that even though the Prophet was most honored, his companions began letters with their own names.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r2.anchor: وروى الربيع عن أنس قال: ما كان أحد أعظم حرمة من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وكان أصحابه إذا كتبوا بدؤوا بأنفسهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r3.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r3.claim: Ibn Sirin reports the Prophet saying Persians start with their leaders, so a man should begin with himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r3.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن أهل فارس إذا كتبوا بدؤوا بعظمائهم فلا يبدأ الرجل إلا بنفسه "

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r4.speaker: أبو الليث
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r4.claim: Abu al-Layth allows starting with the recipient because custom and communal practice can justify it; in his time that was preferable except when writing to one's servant or child.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r4.anchor: ولو بدأ بالمكتوب إليه لجاز لأن الأمة قد اجتمعت عليه وفعلوه لمصلحة رأوا في ذلك، أو نسخ ما كان من قبل فالأحسن في زماننا هذا أن يبدأ بالمكتوب إليه،

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r5.claim: A recipient should answer a letter containing a greeting because a letter from an absent person is like a greeting from someone present.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r5.anchor: وإذا ورد على إنسان كتاب بالتحية أو نحوها ينبغي أن يرد الجواب لأن الكتاب من الغائب كالسلام من الحاضر.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas considered responding to a letter obligatory, just as responding to a greeting is obligatory.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه كان يرى رد الكتاب واجبا كما يرى رد السلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r7.claim: Writers agree on beginning letters with Bismillah and sealing them to avoid suspicion; this practice has textual precedent.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r7.anchor: اتفقوا على كتب «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم» في أول الكتب والرسائل، وعلى ختمها لأنه أبعد من الريبة، وعلى هذا جرى الرسم،

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r8.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r8.claim: Umar says any letter that is not sealed is unfinished or exposed.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r8.anchor: وبه جاء الأثر عن عمر بن الخطاب أنه قال: أيما كتاب لم يكن مختوما فهو أغلف.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r9.claim: A hadith says a letter's nobility is its seal.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r10.speaker: ابن المقفع
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r10.claim: Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ says an unsealed letter to one's brother shows disrespect because sealing completes a letter.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r10.anchor: وقال بعض الأدباء هو ابن المقفع: من كتب إلى أخيه كتابا ولم يختمه فقد استخف به لأن الختم ختم.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r11.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r11.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet made a ring bearing the testimony of faith because non-Arabs would accept only sealed letters; Anas recalls its shine in his hand.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r11.anchor: وقال أنس: لما أراد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يكتب إلى العجم فقيل له: إنهم لا يقبلون إلا كتابا عليه ختم فاصطنع خاتما ونقش على فصه لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r12.claim: With both instances of وإنه read with kasra, either an implied الكلام is understood or the second clause begins a new sentence.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r12.anchor: { وإنه } بالكسر فيهما أي وإن الكلام، أو إن مبتدأ الكلام { بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم }.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r13.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r13.claim: Al-Farra permits both clauses with fatha as apposition to the letter, or as accusative after an omitted preposition explaining its nobility.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r13.anchor: وأجاز الفراء { أنه من سليمان وأنه } بفتحهما جميعا على أن يكونا في موضع رفع بدل من الكتاب

QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r14.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي ومحمد بن السميقع
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r14.claim: Al-Ashhab al-Uqayli and Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqaʿ read ألا تغلوا with ghayn, from a verb meaning to exceed and act arrogantly; it conveys the standard reading's sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:30-31/r14.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي ومحمد بن السميقع: { ألا تغلوا } بالغين المعجمة وروي عن وهب بن منبه من غلا يغلوا إذا تجاوز وتكبر.

RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r6.claim: The queen's words identify and explain the letter she has just called noble, as though she were answering who sent it and what it said.
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r6.anchor: أنه استئناف وتبيين لما ألقى إليها كأنها لما قالت إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم

RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r7.speaker: عبدالله
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r7.claim: Abdullah reads the clause as coordinated with the queen's preceding statement I have received.
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ عبدالله { إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله }

RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r8.claim: In a reading with the two inna clauses opened, one analysis makes the statement an apposition to letter, as if what was delivered was that it came from Solomon.
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r8.anchor: أنه بدل من كتاب كأنه قيل ألقي إلي أنه من سليمان

RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r9.claim: A second analysis understands the clause as saying it is from Solomon and because it begins in God's name, with the basmala explaining its nobility.
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r9.anchor: أن يريد أن من سليمان ولأنه بسم الله كأنها عللت كرمه بكونه من سليمان وتصديره بسم الله

RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r10.speaker: أبي
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r10.claim: Ubayy reads أن من سليمان وأن بسم الله, taking the particles as explanatory; the أن in ألا تعلوا is also explanatory.
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( أن من سليمان وأن بسم الله ) على أن المفسرة

RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r13.claim: Solomon did not put his own name before the basmala: he began with the basmala, while the queen first identified the letter as his and then quoted its contents, so the order belongs to her report.
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r13.anchor: حاشاه من ذلك بل ابتدأ هو ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r14.claim: Prophets write concisely and address only what is needed: people need knowledge before action, and the basmala establishes God as existent, knowing, powerful, living, willing, wise, and merciful.
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r14.anchor: الأنبياء عليهم السلام لا يطيلون بل يقتصرون على المقصود

STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.claim: The account of Solomon's miraculous host and encounter with the Queen of Sheba ends with her embracing faith in the One God.
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.anchor: Solomon with his miraculous host of men, jinn, and birds and his encounter with the Queen of Sheba, who eventually comes before Solomon

STUDYQURAN:27:29/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:29/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:29/r4.claim: Verse 27:30 is the Quran's sole repetition of the full basmalah inside a surah.
STUDYQURAN:27:29/r4.anchor: V. 30 is the only verse in the Quran that repeats the entire basmalah

TAB-FULL:v18p46/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r1.claim: Wahb reports that Solomon’s letter identified its sender and recipient, then called on the queen and her people not to be arrogant and to come submissively; the hoopoe carried it in its leg and dropped it through her sun window.
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r1.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، قال: " كتب، يعني سليمان بن داود مع الهدهد: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، من سليمان بن داود، إلى بلقيس بنت ذي سرح وقومها

TAB-FULL:v18p46/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r2.claim: Qatada’s report describes Bilqis’s lineage and appearance, her large council and location, and the hoopoe’s entry through a locked palace window; it says prophets wrote concise sentences rather than elaborating.
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r2.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة، قال: " بلغني أنها امرأة يقال لها بلقيس، أحسبه قال: ابنة شراحيل، أحد أبويها من الجن

TAB-FULL:v18p46/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Solomon’s letter contained no more than the wording reported in the Qur’an: “it is from Solomon” and “it is in the name of God.”
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: " لم يزد

SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r1.claim: The common reading opens both hamzas with kasra as two answers to the people's implied questions: who sent the letter and what it contains.
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r1.anchor: العامة على كسر الهمزتين على الاستئناف جوابا لسؤال قومها كأنهم قالوا: ممن الكتاب؟ وما فيه؟

SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r2.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh adds a coordinating waw and joins innahu min Sulaymān to the clause in which she says she received the letter.
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r2.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله " وإنه من سليمان " بزيادة واو عاطفة " إنه من سليمان " على قوله: { إني ألقي إلي }.

SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r3.speaker: عكرمة
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r3.claim: ʿIkrimah and Ibn Abī ʿAblah read both hamzas with fatḥa.
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r3.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة وابن أبي عبلة بفتح الهمزتين.

SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r4.claim: With both hamzas open, the clauses can substitute for kitāb by inclusion or full substitution; the author calls this the strongest analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r4.anchor: أحدهما: أنه بدل من " كتاب " بدل اشتمال، أو بدل كل من كل، كأنه قيل: ألقي إلي أنه من سليمان، وأنه كذا وكذا. وهذا هو الأصح.

SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r5.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says the open clauses are governed as a predicate of karīm, but the author finds this weak.
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r5.anchor: والثاني: أنه مرفوع ب " كريم " ذكره أبو البقاء، وليس بالقوي.

SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows an omitted causal lām: the letter is noble because it is from Solomon and begins in God's name.
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r6.anchor: قال الزمشخري: " ويجوز أن تريد: لأنه من سليمان، ولأنه، كأنها عللت كرمه بكونه من سليمان وتصديره باسم الله ".

SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r7.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r7.claim: Makkī reports that al-Farrāʾ allowed the open-hamza form in ordinary speech; the author notes that this is also a transmitted reading.
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r7.anchor: قال مكي: " وأجاز الفراء الفتح فيهما في الكلام " كأنه لم يطلع على أنها قراءة.

SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r8.speaker: أبي
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r8.claim: Ubayy reads both forms with a quiescent nūn: an mif Sulaymān and an bi-smi Allāh.
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبي " أن من سليمان، وأن بسم الله " بسكون النون فيهما.

SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r9.claim: The first analysis of Ubayy's reading is that an is explanatory, since a speech-like expression precedes it.
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r9.anchor: أظهرهما: أنها " أن " المفسرة، لتقدم ما هو بمعنى القول.

SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r10.claim: The alternative makes an a reduced particle with an omitted subject, but this fails Basran rules: its subject must be the pronoun of shaʾn, explained only by a complete clause.
SAMIN-DURR:27:30/r10.anchor: والثاني: أنها المخففة، واسمها محذوف وهذا لا يتمشى على أصول البصريين؛ لأن اسمها لا يكون إلا ضمير شأن،

TABATABAI:27:26-30/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r8.claim: The phrase from Solomon and in God's name explains why the queen calls the letter noble, given her knowledge of Solomon's authority and the divine opening.
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r8.anchor: وقوله { إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم } ظاهره أنه تعليل لكون الكتاب كريما

TABATABAI:27:30-31/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r1.claim: The letter's association with God ennobles it because even idolaters acknowledge God as Lord of lords; sun worshippers among the Sabians honor Him and His attributes, interpreting them as absence of defects such as ignorance, incapacity, death, and cruelty.
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r1.anchor: والوثنيون جميعا قائلون بالله سبحانه يرونه رب الأرباب وإن لم يعبدوه، وعبدة الشمس منهم وهم من شعب الصابئين

TABATABAI:27:30-31/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r2.claim: The letter begins with God's name; its message, rather than a verbatim quotation, is that the recipients must not behave arrogantly toward Solomon and must come submissively.
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r2.anchor: وعلى هذا فالكتاب أي مضمونه هو قوله { أن لا تعلوا علي وأتوني مسلمين } وأن مفسرة

TABATABAI:27:30-31/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r3.speaker: جمع من المفسرين
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r3.claim: Some exegetes treat the statement that the letter is from Solomon as a fresh answer to an implied question, and take the following phrase as a quotation of the letter's text.
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r3.anchor: ومن العجيب ما عن جمع من المفسرين أن قوله { إنه من سليمان } استئناف وقع جوابا لسؤال مقدر

TABATABAI:27:30-31/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r4.claim: That reading makes the explanatory particle in the message redundant; the attempted repair that makes it a verbal noun and the negation non-prohibitive is weak.
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r4.anchor: ويتوجه عليهم أولا وقوع لفظه أن زائدة لا فايدة لها ولذا قال بعضهم إنها مصدرية و { لا } نافية لا ناهية وهو وجه سخيف

TABATABAI:27:30-31/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r6.claim: The explanatory particle introduces the message's meaning: the letter opened with God's name and its content prohibited arrogance and commanded submission; it need not quote the letter verbatim, resolving the apparent objection.
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r6.anchor: أن ظاهر أن المفسرة في قوله { أن لا تعلوا علي } الخ، أنه نقل لمعنى الكتاب ومضمونه لا حكاية متنه

TABRISI:27:27-31/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:27-31/r18.claim: Belqīs explains that Solomon sent the letter and that its written content begins with “In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.”
TABRISI:27:27-31/r18.anchor: معناه أن الكتاب من سليمان وأن المكتوب فيه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

TABRISI:27:27-31/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:27-31/r19.claim: Solomon was the first to begin a letter with the basmala, which Belqīs and her people did not know.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r19.anchor: وأول من استفتح ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم سليمان ع ولم تعرفه هي ولا قومها.

THALABI:v7p204#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p204#3/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
THALABI:v7p204#3/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Solomon added nothing beyond the Qur’an’s concise account of the letter: “It is from Solomon, and it is…”
THALABI:v7p204#3/r1.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: لم يزد سليمان على ما قص الله في كتابه إنه ... وإنه

THALABI:v7p204#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p204#3/r2.speaker: منصور
THALABI:v7p204#3/r2.claim: Mansur says Solomon was the most eloquent in his letters and wrote the least; the concise basmala exemplifies his style.
THALABI:v7p204#3/r2.anchor: قال منصور: كان يقال: كان سليمان أبلغ الناس في كتابه، وأقله إملاء ثم قرأ إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

THALABI:v7p204#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p204#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p204#3/r3.claim: Qatadah says prophets wrote concise sentences and did not write at excessive length.
THALABI:v7p204#3/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: وكذلك الأنبياء عليهم السلام كانت تكتب جملا لا يطيلون ولا يكثرون

THALABI:v7p204#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p204#3/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p204#3/r4.claim: Solomon perfumed the letter with musk and sealed it with his signet ring.
THALABI:v7p204#3/r4.anchor: فلما كتب الكتاب طبعه بالمسك، وختمه بخاتمه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi describes the hoopoe entering through a palace window, crossing seven rooms, placing the sealed letter by the sleeping queen, pecking her awake, and returning to the window; the doors were locked and guards saw no entrant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: لما أتاها الهدهد كانت في قصرها فدار حول القصر وطلب السبيل إليها حتى وصل من كوة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r2.claim: Finding no one had entered, the queen thought the letter had been sent down from heaven.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r2.anchor: فوقع في قلبها أنه ألقي عليها من السماء، فعند ذلك قالت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r3.claim: She opened the letter and read that it was from Solomon son of David to Bilqis daughter of Dhū al-Sharḥ, containing the basmala; she told her attendants it was Solomon's letter and accurately described its writing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r3.anchor: وكانت كاتبة قارئة، فإذا فيه: {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} من سليمان بن داود، إلى بلقيس بنت ذي الشرح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says the queen first thought the letter came from God before reading it; after reading, she said it was from Solomon and contained the basmala.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p222/r4.anchor: ونحو هذا قال السدي؛ قال: لما ألقاه الهدهد في حجرها ظنت أنه من عند الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:28-34/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:28-34/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:28-34/r3.claim: She states that it is from Solomon and begins with “In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate.”
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:28-34/r3.anchor: إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542/r1.claim: “Do not exalt yourselves over me” means do not resist me.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542/r1.anchor: {إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم {30} ألا تعلوا علي} [النمل: 30-31] ، أي: لا تمتنعوا علي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542/r3.claim: Prophets customarily wrote concise sentences without elaboration or verbosity.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542/r3.anchor: قال: وكذلك كانت تكتب الأنبياء جملا لا يطنبون ولا يكثرون.

BURHAN:v1p390/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p390/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p390/r1.claim: The omitted alif in bism signals the name’s elevated, unique rank and its connection to God, whose name gathers all names; the spelling also evokes manifestation and hiddenness.
BURHAN:v1p390/r1.anchor: تنبيها على علوه فى أول رتبة الأسماء وانفراده

BURHAN:v1p390/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p390/r3.speaker: علماء الظاهر
BURHAN:v1p390/r3.claim: The outward scholars explain the omission as abbreviation from frequent use: the alif of ism is dropped only when appended to Allah and preceded by ba according to the majority.
BURHAN:v1p390/r3.anchor: وعلماء الظاهر يقولون للاختصار وكثرة الاستعمال وهو من خصائص الجلالة الشريفة

BURHAN:v1p390/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p390/r4.speaker: الكسائي
BURHAN:v1p390/r4.claim: Al-Kisaʾi does not require the preceding ba and permits deletion in forms such as bism al-malik; the majority requires ba.
BURHAN:v1p390/r4.anchor: ولم يشترط الكسائى الثانى فجوز حذفها كما تحذف فى بسم الملك والجمهور على الأول

BURHAN:v4p415/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p415/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p415/r1.claim: Min first marks the beginning of an extent when paired with ilā, literally or in meaning; in the letter it marks origin from Solomon, with a person standing for a place of origin.
BURHAN:v4p415/r1.anchor: وما نزل منزلته نحو من فلان ومنه ﴿ إنه من سليمان ﴾

FARRA:v2p292/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p292/r1.speaker: أبي
FARRA:v2p292/r1.claim: On Ubayy's reading, the an in the basmala is connected to the following an lā taʿlū, so the message means “I have been sent that you not be arrogant.”
FARRA:v2p292/r1.anchor: هي (أن) التي في قوله (أن لا تعلوا على)

FARRA:v2p292/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p292/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p292/r2.claim: The repeated an can express one underlying clause, as in 23:35, which asks whether they are promised resurrection after becoming dust and bones.
FARRA:v2p292/r2.anchor: فأنكم مكررة ومعناها واحد والله أعلم

MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r6.claim: Bismillah leaves an understood phrase implicit, such as ‘this is in God's name’ or ‘in God's name at the start of everything.’
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r6.anchor: قال: «بسم الله» (27/ 30) ، ففيه ضمير مجازه: هذا بسم الله. أو بسم الله أول كل شىء
